messages:
maya: kicking off a 5% canary for rwd-v6-quant4 across longdoc-heavy cohorts. proposing a percentile-based rollforward leash that checks both latency and fidelity before stepping up.

alex: +1. what are the leash params?

maya: draft: monitor p95 latency, p99 queue_time, delta MRR (nDCG on rerank slice), and hallucination-rate. conditions to allow rollforward: p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.12; global delta_MRR >= -0.005; hallucination_rate <= baseline_halluc * 1.2. otherwise auto-fallback to pinned variant.

sara: can we enforce cohort-level protections? longdocs historically take the hit while shorts improve.

maya: yes. require that no cohort has delta_MRR < -0.01 AND global delta_MRR >= -0.005. protects small but critical slices.

jun: sample noise will be annoying. what's the sample-size/significance logic?

maya: add a smoothing/eval window: only evaluate after min_requests (30k) OR min_time (15m), and require either bootstrap CI significance (p < 0.05) OR the delta persists across 3 consecutive windows.

olivia: quant4 changes batching/CPU-GPU balance; track queue_time p99 too. sometimes dequeue latency jumps even when model p95 stable.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary rwd-v6-quant4 @ 2026-05-01T14:12:00Z — traffic 5% across cohorts. CI-run id: ci-7723

alex: add an immediate escape hatch: if error_rate > baseline * 2 OR p95_latency > baseline_p95 * 1.5 -> immediate fallback, no waiting.

sara: logging: capture anonymized sample request/response pairs for any cohort breaching hallucination threshold so we can triage quickly.

maya: will ship anonymized S3 sampler with retention tags. proto for auto-fallback config: 

```
rollout_leash {
  cohorts: ["longdoc", "rerank", "short"]
  thresholds {
    p95_latency_mul: 1.12
    p99_queue_time_mul: 1.5
    global_mrr_drop: -0.005
    cohort_mrr_drop_cutoff: -0.01
    hallucination_mul: 1.2
    error_rate_mul: 2.0
    min_requests: 30000
    evaluation_window_sec: 900
    consecutive_windows: 3
  }
  immediate_fallback_on { error_rate, p95_latency }
}
```

jun: prefer bootstrap CI over t-test since metric distributions are non-normal; 1000 resamples should be fine.

maya: agree. we'll bootstrap MRR and percentile CIs for latency.

olivia: suggestion: softer thresholds for small-to-medium promotion (5% -> 20%) but require stronger fidelity to move further. proposed step thresholds: 
- 5%->20%: p95_mul <= 1.15, global_mrr_drop >= -0.003, cohort_cutoff >= -0.008
- 20%->50%: p95_mul <= 1.10, global_mrr_drop >= -0.002

alex: automate step promotions and post events to #eng-ml. include a fallback "reason" tag in events for postmortem indexing.

sara: i'll kick off a shadow run with 10k synthetic longdocs (job-9932) to pre-validate quant config. will report in ~20m.

deploy-bot: canary metrics dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/canary/rwd-v6-quant4 (eng access)

jun: if shadow shows >0.7% drop on longdocs abort canary early.

maya: ack. i'll watch dashboard and trigger auto-fallback if leash hits. if thresholds need mid-run adjustment ping me and leave a note here.

olivia: one more ask — include a derived metric: cohort-weighted worst-case delta that flags if any cohort contributes >50% of the total negative MRR impact. helps prioritize triage.

maya: good call, adding cohort_contrib_alert if any cohort_share_of_loss > 0.5. will update config and the runbook.

alex: also add a tiny human-in-loop pause before promoting from 20%->50% (30m notice) so on-call can inspect logs. automation should allow override with audit entry.

sara: shadow results: job-9932 summary: longdocs (10k) delta_nDCG = -0.42% (CI [-0.9%, +0.06%]), rerank slice +0.12%, short prompts +0.9%. noise but borderline on longdocs; will keep an eye.

maya: thanks — borderline but within our 5%->20% rule (require global >= -0.003 would fail though). i'm holding promotion until we have bootstrap p < 0.05 or 3 windows.

olivia: thanks for the leash design — looks pragmatic. ping me if you want me to run additional synthetic variations (KV-warm, multi-turn).

maya: will do. final note: all fallback events will include: timestamp, canary_version, step_percent, metric_snapshot (stringified), and reason_tag.
